rationale: The current best script learns the rank-64 bigram tail late because `bigram_scale` starts at zero, which blocks gradient flow into the bigram weights during the expensive early steps of a 600-second run. A previous warm-start helped but likely paid some random-logit tax. This variant keeps the proven bigram64 path, warms `bigram_scale` to 0.01 so the branch trains from step 1, and zero-initializes `bigram_out.weight` so the initial logits stay exactly neutral instead of noisy. That directly targets short-run tail learning without adding runtime or artifact-size pressure.
title: Zero-Init Warm Bigram Output On Rank64 Tail
